 Raptors’ Allen Graves pick looks even better after early 2026 re-draft 
 Allen Graves was a nice pickup for the Raptors. By Elaine Blum | Nov 20, 2026, 11:00 AM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source October 30, 2026; Toronto, Ontario, CAN; Toronto Raptors Allen Graves (22) looks on against the Orlando Magic during the second half of the Emirates NBA Cup at Scotiabank Arena. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Sousa-Kevin Sousa-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The 19th pick may seem high for a 20-year-old who had only started four games in his lone college season at Santa Clara. Turns out, the Toronto Raptors made a pretty good choice by drafting Allen Graves with their first-round pick. He may never become a big-time star like some of his draft classmates, but he has the makings of a solid, reliable role player, who can postitively impact games in a small role, and the Raptors need that, too. 
--> The 19th pick may seem high for a 20-year-old who had only started four games in his lone college season at Santa Clara. Turns out, the Toronto Raptors made a pretty good choice by drafting Allen Graves with their first-round pick. He may never become a big-time star like some of his draft classmates, but he has the makings of a solid, reliable role player, who can postitively impact games in a small role, and the Raptors need that, too. 
 About one month into the season, Bleacher Report published its first 2026 re-draft . Graves didn’t need to play much or put up crazy numbers to climb four spots to number fifteen. The Chicago Bulls originally drafted Dailyn Swain with that pick. He fell to number 24 in the redraft. 
--> About one month into the season, Bleacher Report published its first 2026 re-draft . Graves didn’t need to play much or put up crazy numbers to climb four spots to number fifteen. The Chicago Bulls originally drafted Dailyn Swain with that pick. He fell to number 24 in the redraft. 
 The re-draft is an early sign that the Raptors got a steal when Graves was available when they made their pick. 
--> The re-draft is an early sign that the Raptors got a steal when Graves was available when they made their pick. 
 Allen Graves has shown promise despite the Raptors’ rough start 
--> Allen Graves has shown promise despite the Raptors’ rough start 
 The Raptors’ season is off to a rough start with a 5-10 record, which has them sitting in ninth place in the Eastern Conference. They have now lost six straight games and haven’t been able to beat a playoff team. A lot of that comes down to injuries. Kawhi Leonard has only played two games, and Scottie Barnes, Jakob Poeltl, Immanuel Quickley, Collin Murray-Boyles, and RJ Barrett have all missed games as well.

They have now lost six straight games and haven’t been able to beat a playoff team. A lot of that comes down to injuries. Kawhi Leonard has only played two games, and Scottie Barnes, Jakob Poeltl, Immanuel Quickley, Collin Murray-Boyles, and RJ Barrett have all missed games as well. 
 Those injuries have created an opportunity for Graves to log meaningful NBA minutes. He averaged almost 15 minutes over his first 15 games and put up 4.6 points, 2.8 rebounds, 0.8 assists, 0.5 steals, and 0.4 blocks per game. 
--> Those injuries have created an opportunity for Graves to log meaningful NBA minutes. He averaged almost 15 minutes over his first 15 games and put up 4.6 points, 2.8 rebounds, 0.8 assists, 0.5 steals, and 0.4 blocks per game. 
 Those numbers don’t jump off the page, but they also don’t tell the whole story . Graves understands that as a rookie on a team full of veteran players hoping to compete for a title soon, he has to do the little things and impact games on the margins. He’s doing that by holding his own defensively and crashing the boards every opportunity he gets. 
--> Those numbers don’t jump off the page, but they also don’t tell the whole story . Graves understands that as a rookie on a team full of veteran players hoping to compete for a title soon, he has to do the little things and impact games on the margins. He’s doing that by holding his own defensively and crashing the boards every opportunity he gets. 
 He may not get many shots up, but he does his best to create opportunities for his teammates by keeping possessions alive. Graves has already grabbed 26 offensive rebounds—second on the team behind Jakob Poeltl and ahead of Barnes, Barrett, and Murray-Boyles who have all played a lot more minutes. 
--> He may not get many shots up, but he does his best to create opportunities for his teammates by keeping possessions alive. Graves has already grabbed 26 offensive rebounds—second on the team behind Jakob Poeltl and ahead of Barnes, Barrett, and Murray-Boyles who have all played a lot more minutes. 
 That effort is impressive, and it will help Graves carve out a long-term role for himself in the NBA. If his 3-point shot begins to fall more consistently soon, he is the perfect role player for the Raptors, and that’s a great get with a draft pick in the lower half of the first round.
